title: Long Horizons — Compaction & Notes
subtitle: Sessions rot before windows fill: compaction that preserves decisions, and notes that move memory out of the window entirely
topics: Context pressure — why append-only sessions degrade long before the limit
Compaction — distill history into a summary that keeps decisions and open issues
What compaction must preserve — decisions, unresolved questions, load-bearing ids
Structured note-taking — the write strategy as persistent external memory
Choosing between them — conversational continuity vs milestone iteration

analogy.title: The Detective's Case Board
analogy.text: A detective's desk accumulates everything — transcripts, coffee-stained tips, three copies of the same alibi. By week two the desk is unusable: not because it's full, but because the signal is buried, and she re-interviews a witness she already cleared. So twice a day she rewrites the case board: suspects ruled out (with why), open leads, the exact license plate — and clears the desk. The board is compaction. Her notebook — filed at the precinct, survives even if the desk burns — is note-taking. The desk is your context window; the skill is knowing what goes on the board, what goes in the notebook, and what goes in the bin.

antiPatterns: Append-only sessions — every turn and tool dump accumulates until the goal is buried mid-window; the model re-asks answered questions (the kit's M24 lab watches a step get redone)
Compaction that keeps the wrong things — summarizing the pleasantries and dropping 'PA-1004 is still unresolved' preserves tone and loses the case
Notes nobody reads back — writing memory without a retrieval habit is a diary, not a memory system; the write strategy is only half of write/select

sections.title: Pressure, Not Capacity, Is the Enemy
sections.body:
Ask MedFlow's copilot ten questions in naive mode and watch the session strip: every call re-carries the growing transcript, and the history layer climbs while answer quality has nowhere to go but down. This is context rot in its session form — 'performance degradation as context expands, despite increased data availability' [ANTHROPIC-CE] — and the literature is blunt that it starts well below the window limit [ROT-LIT]. The failure signal is signal-to-noise, not size.

The session strip's sparkline makes pressure visible: naive slopes upward forever. The two techniques in this module exist to bend that curve flat.

sections.title: Compaction: Rewrite the Case Board
sections.body:
Compaction distills the transcript-so-far into a compact summary and replaces the raw history with it. What must survive is precise [ANTHROPIC-CE]: decisions made ('PA-1002 needs the EMG before re-scoring'), open issues ('awaiting Dr. Osei's note'), and load-bearing identifiers — while redundant tool dumps and resolved detours are exactly what gets discarded. Notice this is U07's ladder applied to history: prune the resolved, extract the decisions verbatim, abstract the chatter — and the same fidelity discipline applies.

The parent KG course's M02B lab measured this shape on a rotted transcript: raw 3,131 tokens → compressed 1,551 at full key-fact survival. Compaction is not optional hygiene for long sessions; it is the difference between a session that converges and one that buries its own goal.

sections.title: Notes: Memory Outside the Window
sections.body:
The notes mode goes further: after each answer it writes structured notes — facts established, per member and request — to a store outside the window, and subsequent asks load relevant notes instead of replaying the transcript. That is the canonical write strategy [LC-WSCI]: 'saving it outside the context window to help the agent perform the task,' then selecting it back on demand.

The receipts show the payoff: notes answers Q1 at 141 tokens and holds a 198 median across all ten questions at 100% correctness (replay grid) — because a note like M-2001: PA-1001 APPROVED, PA-1004 MANUAL_REVIEW is smaller than the conversation that established it. Notes survive what history cannot: the session strip flattens, and the memory would survive even a fresh session. The parent KG course's OKF log.md is this same pattern at repository scale.

sections.title: Which One, When
sections.body:
Anthropic's task-context alignment table gives the decision rule [ANTHROPIC-CE]: compaction fits extensive back-and-forth needing conversational continuity — the thread matters, so distill it. Note-taking fits iterative work with identifiable milestones — a review queue worked one request at a time, where established facts matter but the conversation that established them does not. (The third column, sub-agent isolation, is U09.)

In MedFlow terms: a clinician debating one borderline determination wants compaction; a reviewer clearing the queue wants notes. Both bend the pressure curve; they differ in what they promise to preserve — the thread versus the facts.

sections.title: A Compactor That Keeps What Matters
sections.code:
# Compaction = U07's ladder applied to conversation history.
# (Numbers cited: bench/results/fullgrid-compact.csv, synthetic-pre-recording.)

def compact(turns: list[dict], keep_recent: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    old, recent = turns[:-keep_recent], turns[-keep_recent:]

    decisions  = [t["text"] for t in old if t.get("kind") == "decision"]
    open_items = [t["text"] for t in old if t.get("kind") == "open"]
    # resolved detours and raw tool dumps are the compaction target
    dropped    = sum(1 for t in old if t.get("kind") in ("chatter", "tool_dump", "resolved"))

    board = ("CASE BOARD (compacted):\n"
             + "DECISIONS:\n  " + "\n  ".join(decisions or ["none"]) + "\n"
             + "OPEN:\n  " + "\n  ".join(open_items or ["none"])
             + f"\n({dropped} routine turns discarded)")

    # fidelity, U07-style: decisions and open items survive verbatim
    for t in old:
        if t.get("kind") in ("decision", "open"):
            assert t["text"] in board, f"compaction lost: {t['text']!r}"
    return [{"kind": "summary", "text": board}] + recent

turns = [
    {"kind": "chatter",  "text": "hi, looking at the queue"},
    {"kind": "tool_dump", "text": "...4KB of raw queue JSON..."},
    {"kind": "decision", "text": "PA-1002: wait for EMG before re-scoring"},
    {"kind": "resolved", "text": "eligibility confusion - resolved, tier covers it"},
    {"kind": "open",     "text": "PA-1004: conservative-mgmt window ends 2026-09-23"},
    {"kind": "chatter",  "text": "ok next"},
    {"kind": "decision", "text": "PA-1010: borderline 50 - keep in review"},
]
for t in compact(turns):
    print(t["text"][:80])
# Seven turns become one board + two recent turns. The assertion is the
# case board's nurse-check: lose an open item and it refuses to ship.

sections.question: A 40-turn review session starts re-asking questions answered at turn 6, at only ~60% window utilization. WHY does adding more window not fix this?
options: A. It would fix it — the window is simply too small

B. The failure is signal-to-noise, not capacity: the answer at turn 6 is buried under 34 turns of accumulation, and a bigger window just buries it deeper — the fix is compaction or notes, not headroom
C. The model's memory expires after 30 turns
D. Re-asking is correct behavior for freshness
sections.explanation: Context rot bites below the limit [ROT-LIT]; the kit's M24 lab watches an append-only loop redo a completed step for exactly this reason. Pressure is cured by changing what the window carries — the case board, not a bigger desk.

sections.question: A reviewer clears the queue one request at a time across a long shift. WHEN is notes mode the better fit than compaction?
options: B. Here — milestone-style work needs the established facts (statuses, scores) but not the conversational thread; notes carry facts at ~198 median tokens while compaction still re-carries a distilled thread
C. Only if the API key has no cache access
D. When answers must cite the conversation verbatim
sections.explanation: Task-context alignment [ANTHROPIC-CE]: compaction ↔ conversational continuity, notes ↔ identifiable milestones. Queue-clearing is milestones; the note 'M-2001: PA-1001 APPROVED, PA-1004 MANUAL_REVIEW' outlives and out-compresses the thread that established it (Q9 notes: 167 tok, PASS — replay grid).

sections.title: What Goes Wrong
items: Compacting at the cliff — waiting until the window is nearly full means the compactor itself runs in a degraded context; compact on a cadence, not in a panic
Self-summarization in place — asking the main model to summarize the very context it is drowning in; run compaction as its own clean call (the kit's M12 gotcha)
Note sprawl — appending every observation turns the notebook into a second rotting window; notes are structured facts, not a transcript copy

takeaway: Long sessions are saved by changing what the window carries — compact the thread when continuity matters, write notes when only the facts do — and the pressure curve on the session strip tells you it worked.
labUnderstand: Run the same 6-question review session in naive and notes modes and watch the two sparklines: naive's climbs monotonically while notes flattens near ~200 tokens per call. You annotate exactly which layer stopped growing and why.
labBuild: With Claude writing the code, build session_pressure.py: replay a scripted 8-turn session in both modes, chart per-call history-layer tokens, then add a compactor with the decisions/open-items fidelity assertion. Break it on purpose by compacting away an open item and watch the assertion refuse.
